title: POC integration orchestration - SDK/OpenAPI compatibility with CascadeWare
summary: Kickoff scoping for a 6-week POC: define success criteria (latency/cost/accuracy), workload sizing (concurrency, token budgets), benchmark plan (p50/p95, stability runs), integration approach for SDK and OpenAI-compatible endpoints, function/tool calling and structured outputs. Agreement to run initial micro-benchmarks next week and exchange security docs.
action_items: Aisha - share sample workload trace and 2 weeks of production logs (anonymized) by 2026-07-26
Miguel - provide benchmark harness repo link + runbook and suggested instance configs by 2026-07-24
Priya - draft OpenAPI mapping for CascadeWare's current inference calls and share example mapping.json by 2026-07-28
Tom - confirm legal/ procurement timeline and if KMS/HSM is required by 2026-07-30
next_steps: Redwood to run a 2-day micro-benchmark (latency p50/p95, token throughput) against a representative snapshot - target start 2026-07-24
Customer to provide sanitized traces+SLOs and current cost per 1M tokens baseline
Schedule a security deep-dive (Priya + Security SME) the week after benchmarks
Follow-up sync to review results and decide Hosted vs Dedicated by 2026-08-05
transcript:
[00:00] Julia (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick intros?
[00:06] Aisha (CascadeWare): Hi, Aisha here, Head of ML at CascadeWare. We're the team building the customer support summarization and routing product.
[00:13] Tom (CTO): Tom here - overall infrastructure and procurement.
[00:16] Ben (Platform Eng): Ben, infra.
[00:18] Miguel (Redwood SE): Miguel from Redwood, I handle benchmarks and infra tuning.
[00:21] Julia: Cool, the goal today is to scope a POC focused on integration between your system and Redwood's runtime — specifically SDK integration and OpenAI-compatible endpoints, plus function-calling and structured output. We'll cover success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks and timeline.
[00:40] Aisha: Sounds good. A couple quick things up front: our main constraints are 100ms p50 for short replies, p95 under 400ms is ideal, and cost needs to be no more than roughly 30% above our current managed provider spend during pilot. Also data residency for EU customers matters.
[00:58] Miguel: Great, that gives us targets. Can you describe the workload shape? bursty? steady? tokens per request?
[01:05] Aisha: It's pretty bursty - support volume spikes after product releases. Average prompt is 220 tokens in, model generates ~120 tokens. Peak concurrency ~120 active requests, steady 15-25 at off-peak.
[01:18] Ben: Adding that our traffic goes through a routing layer that does pre/post processing. We can insert SDK calls server-side or call an OpenAPI endpoint - preference is server-side to keep PII off the client.
[01:30] Julia: Understood. For the POC we usually recommend two parallel tracks: 1) short integration path using OpenAI-compatible endpoints (fast to wire) and 2) deeper SDK integration to exercise KV caching, batching and function calling if you need tool orchestration.
[01:45] Tom: What's the difference in effort? We have one backend engineer to spare for this sprint.
[01:50] Priya (SE): OpenAI-compatible endpoints are typically the quickest — you can swap existing calls with minimal code. SDK gives more control: persistent connections, better batching, direct KV cache reuse which helps cost/latency. I'd estimate 2-3 days for an initial OpenAPI proof-of-compatibility and 1-2 weeks for full SDK integration including function-calling hooks.
[02:11] Aisha: We're particularly interested in structured output for routing decisions — we need consistent JSON with fields for intent, priority_score, and recommended_route. How deterministic can that be?
[02:22] Miguel: We'll recommend schema-based structured output with Redwood's structured instruction support and a small eval set to measure extraction accuracy (precision/recall on fields). For POC success criteria we can set thresholds, eg intent F1 > 0.88, priority_score correlation > 0.9 with your ground truth, latency targets as Aisha mentioned.
[02:43] Speaker 4: Sorry, can I ask about function calling? We have several internal routing services and external enrichment calls.
[02:49] Priya: Function calling can orchestrate these external lookups in a deterministic way. For POC we'll mock a subset of those services and demonstrate end-to-end tool flows. The SDK has built-in support for function/tool-call sequences and automatic fallbacks if a tool fails.
[03:05] Ben: Any constraints around VPC or private networking?
[03:08] Julia: For enterprise customers like you, Redwood Private supports VPC peering or private endpoints. For the POC we typically start hosted to validate correctness and benchmarks and then spin up a Private VPC trial if you need isolation. If KMS/HSM is required we can include that in the Private option; it adds procurement steps.
[03:28] Tom: Procurement is sensitive — if we can start hosted and collect metrics, that'll help our business case. But we'll need SOC2 and SSO/SAML docs.
[03:36] Priya: We'll share SOC2 artifact links and our security whitepaper; schedule a security-only session after benchmarks.
[03:44] Aisha: On benchmarks - what do you recommend we measure?
[03:47] Miguel: We'll measure p50/p95 latency for cold and warmed KV cache, tokens-per-second throughput for different instance types, cost per 1k tokens for each config, and correctness metrics for structured outputs. We'll run stability runs (6–12 hours) to check tail performance and GC/restarts.
[04:06] Aisha: Cold and warmed cache - what's a warmed cache scenario for us?
[04:09] Miguel: Warming means KV cache populated with recent conversation context or embeddings to avoid recomputing. For conversational routing (short context) warmed path often halves token compute. We'll simulate realistic prefixes from your traces.
[04:22] Julia: Speaking of traces, action item: Aisha will share a sanitized trace sample so we can build the benchmark payloads.
[04:28] Tom: We'll need to anonymize PII — can you accept masked logs?
[04:31] Miguel: Yes, masked logs are fine; we only need token distributions and timing.
[04:35] Aisha: We'll have that by Monday.
[04:38] Speaker 4: How will you report results? What artifacts?
[04:41] Priya: We produce a benchmark spreadsheet with p50/p95, cost estimates per 1M tokens, suggested quantization/instance options, and a short runbook for integrating the SDK. We'll also include a canary rollout playbook for Dedicated or Private deployments.
[04:56] Ben: About quantization — do you recommend 8-bit? Any accuracy loss?
[04:59] Miguel: For your summarization workload, 8-bit quantization on recent T4/RTX-class variants is usually a sweet spot; we include quality regression checks in the harness. If you need highest fidelity we can run fp16 comparisons. We surface quality delta in the spreadsheet.
[05:13] Aisha: Timeline — we have a tentative 6-week window for a POC to drive procurement decision. Can Redwood align?
[05:20] Julia: Yes: Week 1: onboarding and micro-benchmarks; Week 2-3: SDK integration and structured-output tuning; Week 4: longer stability runs and cost optimization; Week 5: security deep-dive and procurement artifacts; Week 6: final report and recommended deployment (hosted vs dedicated). We'll be flexible.
[05:38] Tom: That works, but we need an internal demo by end of Week 3.
[05:42] Priya: We can plan an interim demo of the SDK integration after initial tuning (end of Week 3).
[05:48] Aisha: Ok. Are there any blockers we should surface now?
[05:51] Miguel: The main blocker is representative traces. Second is if you require HSM for key management that pushes the security timeline. Third, if you insist on on-prem in the POC that's a larger lift.
[06:03] Ben: Noted.
[06:05] Speaker 4: One more thing — compatibility with our existing observability (Datadog) and tracing?
[06:10] Julia: Redwood Console has tracing hooks and can emit spans to Datadog; we'll include instrumentation guidance in the runbook.
[06:18] Tom: Pricing signals — can you give a rough cost delta between hosted and dedicated for our scale?
[06:23] Miguel: Very rough: for your peak profile, Hosted may cost ~20-40% more per token but gives no infra ops; Dedicated reserved capacity usually lowers unit cost if you can commit to a baseline. We'll quantify this after the benchmark.
[06:36] Aisha: Any other integration details — SDK languages supported?
[06:40] Priya: We have official SDKs for Python, Node.js, and a lightweight Java client. OpenAPI-compatible endpoints support curl/HTTP or existing OpenAI-style SDKs for quick trials.
[06:51] Ben: Good. For function calling, do we need to remodel our enrichment calls?
[06:55] Miguel: You can map existing enrichment endpoints into function call definitions; for POC we'll mock 2-3 calls and show end-to-end routing.
[07:04] Julia: Alright let's recap. Actions: Aisha share traces; Miguel provide benchmark repo; Priya deliver OpenAPI mapping; Redwood will run a 2-day micro-benchmark starting 2026-07-24; schedule security deep-dive after results.
[07:20] Aisha: Great. Also please send your SOC2 link and a sample runbook.
[07:25] Priya: Will do.
[07:27] Tom: Thanks everyone.
[07:29] Julia: Thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites and links. End.
